newsitem.title: USA: NYC gets Dillon Read to stay, more aid for new jobs.
newsitem.headline: NYC gets Dillon Read to stay, more aid for new jobs.

text.p: New York City on Monday said the investment bank Dillon, Read & Co, which had been considering moving to Connecticut, agreed to stay and possibly more than double its 620 employees.

While the investment bank will get $3.65 million of aid for agreeing to remain instead of relocating to Stamford, the city will only contribute $1.15 million of this amount, a sum it expects to recoup in 2.4 months.
Dillon, Read, which pays the city about $16.6 million in taxes each year, will get the rest of the aid from a combination of state sales tax exemptions and energy rebates.
And the city is offering the investment bank an additional amount of as much as $2.15 million if the firm succeeds in adding the 664 new jobs that it projects.

Calling the investment bank one of America's oldest and most prestigious, Mayor Rudolph Giuliani in prepared remarks added "It is because of companies like Dillon, Read that New York City is able to maintain its status as the financial capital of the world."
The firm also agreed to keep its emergency disaster recovery center in Long Island City.

The Giuliani Administration said that counting Dillon, Read, it has persuaded 19 major companies to remain, saving 48,564 jobs. These firms, which are expected to add 16,434 new jobs, are expected to pay the city $724.3 million a year in taxes for the next 10 to 20 years.
